title: How a block of ice becomes a fridge (v4)
lines: Drop a block of ice in a wooden box. Congratulations, you've built a fridge.
But by tomorrow, the ice is a puddle, and your milk has gone sour.
You need cold that never melts. Ever stepped out of a shower and shivered?
That's water evaporating off your skin, and stealing its heat.
So you run a copper pipe through the box, filled with a liquid that boils below freezing.
As it boils, it sucks the heat right out of your milk. This is the evaporator.
But once it boils into gas, it just escapes into the air.
So you seal the loop, and squeeze the gas with a pump. This is the compressor.
But squeezing gas makes it scorching hot.
So you snake that hot pipe up the back, and the heat escapes into your kitchen. This is the condenser.
Ever noticed the sides of your fridge feel warm? That's this, hiding in the walls.
As the heat leaves, the gas turns back into liquid. But it's squeezed too tight to boil.
So you force it through a copper tube thinner than spaghetti. This is the capillary tube.
Like a spray can, the pressure drops, and it turns freezing cold again.
But now the loop never stops, and your milk freezes solid and cracks the bottle.
So a sensor cuts the pump just above freezing. This is the thermostat.
That's the hum you hear randomly stop at night.
And here's the twist: your fridge never made cold. It just pumps heat from your milk into your kitchen.
Wrap it in foam and steel. Congratulations, you've built a fridge. Unless you'd rather just...
